questions.rank: Which of these skills, if any, is the right one to load to help with the user's latest request?
questions.rerank: Exactly one of these skills is the right one to load for the user's latest request. Which one? Read what each actually does, not just its name.
questions.gateActs: Is the assistant being asked to act on the user's files, accounts, devices, or online services, rather than only to explain or advise?
questions.gateProcedure: Would a careful expert answering this consult a specific documented procedure or set of commands, rather than answering from general understanding?
questions.gateProse: Could a knowledgeable generalist fully satisfy this request in prose, with no tools, no documentation, and no access to the user's files or accounts?
questions.advisory: Does this request ask for creative or advisory work on the user's software project — designing, planning, brainstorming, reviewing, or dispatching development work — where a documented process should guide the assistant, rather than a specific mechanical change?
questions.gateMechanical: Is this a small, self-contained mechanical step, such as renaming, editing a line, bumping a value, reading a file, running one command, or calling one named tool, that needs no documented process or workflow?
questions.fits: Does the skill '{{name}}' do the specific thing the user's request asks for?

questions.delegate: Would this request be better handed to a subagent, because it needs broad searching or reading across many files, several independent parallel tasks, or an independent review, rather than a focused change the main agent can make directly?
questions.pick: Which subagent is the right one to hand this request to, or none if the main agent should handle it directly?

agents.noneLabel: none — the main agent handles this directly

builtin.description: Read-only search across many files or directories; returns conclusions, not file dumps
Designs an implementation plan and weighs architecture trade-offs
Researches open questions and runs multi-step tasks independently

agents.hintDefault:

This is cheap, mechanical work. Hand it to the jev_delegate_light tool (it runs on a low-cost model with maximum thinking) instead of doing it yourself, then check its result.
</system_one_agents>

questions.tier: How demanding is this coding request for the AI model that has to carry it out?
questions.external: Does this request need an external service, a browser, a database, or a third-party API, beyond the project's own files and the shell?
questions.effort: How much careful step-by-step reasoning does this coding request need before the AI model acts?

criteria.light: light: low-stakes work where spending many tokens does not matter and deep reasoning is not needed, at any size: mechanical or repetitive changes such as fixing lint or type errors, renames, formatting, comments or boilerplate across a whole codebase, simple lookups, and short factual questions
criteria.standard: standard: ordinary coding work with a clear goal, such as implementing a small feature, fixing a bug in one place, writing tests, or explaining how some code works
criteria.heavy: heavy: hard work where mistakes are costly and deep reasoning is needed, such as designing an architecture, hunting a subtle or cross-cutting bug, a large refactor, security-sensitive changes, or vague requirements that need judgment

effortCriteria.low: low: a quick answer or an obvious edit that needs almost no reasoning
effortCriteria.medium: medium: ordinary work where a little planning helps
effortCriteria.high: high: tricky logic, several interacting parts, or edge cases that must be thought through
effortCriteria.xhigh: xhigh: a very hard problem that needs long, careful reasoning

questions.claim: Does the latest assistant message assert that the work is complete, done, or finished?
questions.checkRan: Has an automated check (tests, build, lint, or a re-read of the changed artifact) been run against this change in this session?
questions.checkPassed: Did that check pass? Count failing, incomplete, or stale pre-change runs as not passed.

control.hint:
<system_one_control>
Before finishing: run the relevant check for this change, or state explicitly that no check exists. Do not claim completion without evidence.
</system_one_control>

questions.next: Which single tool is the best next step for the agent to make progress?
questions.needsTool: Does making progress on the last step require calling a tool?

hints.noTool: No tool is needed for this step; answer directly.
hints.narrowed: The tool list is already narrowed for this step; do not deliberate about tool choice, act.
hints.fallback: If none of these fit, say what you need in your reply instead of guessing.
